transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
My mind keeps jumping to every little thing around me, and I can’t stay focused on what I’m supposed to be doing anymore. It's really starting to mess with my ability to get my work done.

Have you had trouble paying attention or staying organized since childhood, like in school, or did this mainly start more recently? Also, do you feel tense and worry a lot about many different things?

This focus trouble is actually pretty recent, starting about seven months ago when I switched to a regional sales job. As for worrying, I've had some anxiety before, but right now it's more that my mind is constantly racing and feeling completely wired rather than just tense worrying.

Along with feeling mentally wired, have you been feeling down or losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy for most of the day, nearly every day? If so, has that been going on for at least two weeks?

No, I haven't been feeling down or losing interest in things at all. If anything, it's the exact opposite—I feel highly energetic and interested in way too many things at once. My main issue is that I just can't seem to slow down enough to actually focus on one task.

Have you ever had a separate period in the past when you felt unusually depressed for at least two weeks, with low mood or loss of interest most of the day? Or have all of your episodes been only times of feeling overly energetic or wired?

I don't recall ever having separate periods where I felt deeply depressed or lost interest in things for weeks at a time. For me, the main struggle has really just been these recent months of feeling completely wired, energetic, and too distracted to focus.
During these past several months, have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling full of energy the next day? About how many hours are you sleeping on average?

Yes, I'm only sleeping about three to four hours a night, but I wake up completely wired and full of energy before my alarm even goes off. I honestly feel like sleep is just a waste of daylight when I could be using that time to plan for new clients or work on my woodworking and photography projects.

During this energized period, have your symptoms become severe enough to cause major problems at work or in relationships, lead to risky or impulsive behavior, or make you feel out of touch with reality, like hearing things or having beliefs others say aren’t true?

Yes, it has caused major trouble—I nearly lost a key account, my boss warned me about my erratic hours, and my wife is furious that I'm missing family events and racking up credit card debt on woodworking and photo gear. I don't hear voices or anything like that, but I have been convinced that I'm the only one who can save our company's sales region if everyone would just get out of my way.

This supports keeping F30.1 and does not currently suggest adding depressive, anxiety, or childhood-onset attentional conditions.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a recent 7-month period of persistently elevated/expansive activation with markedly decreased need for sleep, racing mind, increased energy, excessive involvement in multiple projects, grandiose thinking, distractibility, and significant occupational, financial, and marital impairment. There is no evidence of a depressive episode, and psychotic symptoms were denied. This is most consistent with a manic episode without psychotic symptoms.
